text: For m in a subcomodule N, its right coaction lies in the image of N⊗C→M⊗C. This exposes exactly the stored stability property, matching [Milne’s subcomodule definition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) over fields. Over a general semiring it means image membership; injectivity of that tensor map is not silently assumed. Checks pass: [coact_mem_tensor_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L186), [rid_lTensor_coact_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L151).
Checks stability of the full submodule.
Checks stability under contraction by a coefficient functional.

Constructing a subcomodule from a submodule N and its coaction-stability proof retains precisely N as the carrier. The constructor adds a property rather than enlarging the set. This matches [Milne’s subcomodule definition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95); over semirings, stability is stated using the tensor-map image and does not itself install an inherited coaction. Checks pass: [mem_ofSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L181), [mem_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L114).
Checks the corresponding membership equivalence.
Checks passage to the underlying module preserves elements.

An element belongs to the subcomodule built from N exactly when it belongs to N. The supplied stability proof changes no elements or scalar operations. This is the carrier interpretation of [Milne’s subcomodule definition](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), extended to the native semiring tensor-image convention without assuming that every stable subtype already has a coaction. Checks pass: [ofSubmodule_carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L176), [coact_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Basic.lean#L144).
Checks the whole carrier is unchanged.
Checks the constructed subobject exposes its stability condition.

The underlying module of the inverse-image subcomodule is the ordinary linear preimage: precisely the m with f(m) in B. The native construction is over a commutative ring and assumes C flat. [Flat tensor exactness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9) ensures this preimage is coaction-stable; f need not be injective, and neither ambient module must be finitely generated. Checks pass: [mem_comap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L105), [comap_bot_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L123).
Checks the elementwise preimage condition.
Checks the zero-subobject case gives the kernel.

The inverse image of B under a comodule morphism f consists of m with f(m) in B. Over a commutative ring, flatness of C preserves the kernel of M→N/B after tensoring, proving coaction stability. This uses [Stacks’ exactness characterization of flatness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9); f need not be surjective. Checks pass: [mem_comap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L105), [map_le_iff_le_comap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L130).
Checks the defining membership condition.
Checks the image/preimage adjunction.

Membership in the inverse-image subcomodule means exactly that f(m) belongs to the given target subcomodule. This equivalence unfolds the linear preimage. Its surrounding ring and flat-C hypotheses belong to the stability construction, justified by [tensor exactness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9); the membership test itself imposes no choice of preimage or surjectivity of f. Checks pass: [comap_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L117), [comap_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L168).
Checks the inverse image of the full subcomodule.
Checks inverse image along the identity.

The kernel of a comodule morphism is its zero fibre, equipped with subcomodule stability. Over the stated commutative ring, flatness of C makes tensoring preserve the linear kernel, as in [Stacks 10.39.1](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9). Thus the carrier is the ordinary kernel; f need not be injective or surjective, and its domain need not be finitely generated. Checks pass: [mem_ker](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L196), [zero_mem_ker](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L203).
Checks membership means f(m)=0.
Checks the zero vector belongs.

Forgetting the kernel’s subcomodule structure gives exactly the kernel of the underlying linear map. The subcomodule is defined as the inverse image of zero, so there is no extra closure operation. Flatness of C over the commutative base ring supplies the needed stability through [tensor exactness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9). Checks pass: [comap_bot_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L123), [mem_ker](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L196).
Checks inverse image of zero is the linear kernel.
Checks the same identification elementwise.

A vector belongs to the kernel subcomodule exactly when its image under f is zero. This identifies the stored stable submodule with the usual linear kernel. The surrounding flat-C hypothesis ensures that kernel is a subcomodule by [tensor exactness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9); no additional condition on the vector or on the image of f is hidden. Checks pass: [zero_mem_ker](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L203), [le_ker_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L208).
Checks the zero-vector case.
Checks the corresponding vanishing criterion for an entire subcomodule.

Taking the inverse image of the zero subcomodule and then forgetting its structure yields the linear kernel of f. Elementwise, both sides say f(m)=0. The ring and flat-C assumptions ensure the inverse image is coaction-stable through [tensor exactness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9), while this equality itself only identifies the unchanged underlying subset. Checks pass: [ker_toSubmodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L184), [mem_ker](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Comap.lean#L196).
Checks the packaged kernel uses this module.
Checks the zero-fibre description.

Corestricting f to a subcomodule P known to contain every f(m) leaves its value unchanged after inclusion back into the ambient module. This is the inherited-subcomodule interpretation in [Milne](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The native semiring construction assumes flat C so P carries the inherited coaction; it does not assert that f surjects onto P. Checks pass: [codRestrict_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L288), [subtype_comp_codRestrict](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L302).
Checks the underlying ordinary linear corestriction.
Checks composition with inclusion recovers f.

The comodule inclusion of N into M sends each element to its underlying ambient vector. This is the literal inclusion associated with the inherited subcomodule in [Milne](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). The native semiring statement retains flatness of C to construct N’s coaction; it does not replace the inclusion by an abstract isomorphic copy. Checks pass: [subtype_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L235), [subtype_rTensor_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L214).
Checks the complete underlying linear map.
Checks compatibility with the ambient coaction.

For the inherited right coaction on N, applying inclusion to its first tensor factor recovers the ambient coaction of the same vector. This is restriction of coaction as in [Milne](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). Flatness of C makes N⊗C→M⊗C injective, so that inherited tensor is uniquely determined; the coefficient factor remains unchanged. Checks pass: [induced_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L208), [subtype_rTensor_inducedCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L80).
Checks the installed coaction is the constructed lift.
Checks the lift’s ambient-image identity.

The underlying linear map of the subcomodule inclusion is exactly the subtype inclusion N→M. Its extra structure proves compatibility with the right coactions; it changes no vector. This agrees with [Milne’s inherited subcomodule](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95), with flat C explicitly retained over the broader commutative-semiring base. Checks pass: [subtype_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L240), [subtype_rTensor_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L214).
Checks evaluation on a vector.
Checks the coaction-intertwining identity.

Including the first factor of the constructed coaction N→N⊗C gives the original coaction evaluated in M. This is the defining restriction identity for [Milne’s subcomodule](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95). In the native semiring setting, flatness means tensoring preserves injections; it makes this lift unique rather than an arbitrary choice of tensor representative. Checks pass: [subtype_rTensor_comp_inducedCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L89), [induced_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L208).
Checks the same identity as an equality of linear maps.
Checks this lift supplies the inherited coaction.

Writing ι:N→M for inclusion, the induced coaction satisfies (ι⊗id_C)∘ρ_N=ρ_M∘ι. This expresses the [subcomodule restriction identity](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=95) on all vectors at once. Flat C over the commutative semiring guarantees the lift exists uniquely; the notation rTensor C leaves the right coefficient factor unchanged. Checks pass: [subtype_rTensor_inducedCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L80), [induced_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Induced.lean#L208).
Checks the pointwise formula.
Checks the induced map is the installed coaction.

For q:M→M/N, the quotient coaction satisfies ρ̄∘q=(q⊗id_C)∘ρ. This is the defining descent identity and determines ρ̄ because q is surjective. Stability of N makes the right side vanish on N. The [right-exact tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DF) works over the stated commutative ring without a flatness assumption on C. Checks pass: [quotientCoact_mk](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L79), [mkQ_surjective](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L238).
Checks the identity on quotient representatives.
Checks representatives determine the whole quotient.

The quotient coaction sends [m] to (q⊗id_C)ρ(m). Stability puts ρ(N) in the tensor image of N⊗C, which q⊗id_C kills, so the value is independent of the representative. This uses [tensor right exactness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DF) over the commutative base ring; no flatness of C or choice of representatives is required. Checks pass: [quotientCoact_mk](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L79), [quotientCoact_comp_mkQ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L87).
Checks the representative formula.
Checks the descent identity as linear maps.

The quotient M/N inherits the right coaction [m]↦(q⊗id_C)ρ(m). Stability ensures well-definedness, and checking on representatives transfers coassociativity and the counit identity from M, matching [EGNO 1.20.2](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). The native ring-level construction uses tensor right exactness and requires no flatness of the coefficient coalgebra. Checks pass: [quotient_coact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L210), [quotientCoact_comp_mkQ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L87).
Checks the installed operation is the descended map.
Checks compatibility with the quotient projection.

The underlying linear map of the quotient comodule morphism is precisely the ordinary projection M→M/N. Its added compatibility proof is ρ̄q=(q⊗id_C)ρ, in the [right-comodule convention](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). The native statement assumes a commutative ring and a coaction-stable N; it imposes no flatness on C. Checks pass: [mkQ_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L228), [quotientCoact_comp_mkQ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L87).
Checks vectors are sent to their quotient classes.
Checks the coaction compatibility.

The quotient comodule map kills exactly the vectors of N: q(m)=0 iff m∈N. This is the ordinary module-quotient kernel rule for the [descended tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DF); no flatness of C is needed. Naming that kernel as a separate kernel subcomodule elsewhere introduces flatness, but this membership criterion does not. Checks pass: [mkQ_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L228), [ker_mkQ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L324).
Checks q(m) is the ordinary quotient class.
Checks the bundled kernel equality in the separate flat-C API.

This is the ordinary quotient projection q:M→M/N packaged as a comodule morphism. Its intertwining equation ρ̄q=(q⊗id_C)ρ follows from the definition of quotient coaction, using the [right-comodule convention](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/tenscat1.pdf#page=41). Coaction stability of N ensures descent over the commutative ring; no flatness hypothesis on C is added. Checks pass: [mkQ_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L228), [quotientCoact_comp_mkQ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L87).
Checks the projection’s value.
Checks it intertwines the two coactions.

Every element of the quotient comodule M/N is represented by some vector of M, so the quotient morphism is surjective. This is actual surjectivity of its underlying function, not a choice of canonical representative. It supports the universal property of the [quotient tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DF) without requiring C flat. Checks pass: [mkQ_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L228), [liftQ_unique](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L315).
Checks the map sends vectors to quotient classes.
Checks representatives determine a descended comodule morphism uniquely.

The coaction on the class of m is (q⊗id_C)ρ(m): only the module factor is passed to the quotient. Stability makes this formula independent of m’s representative, as in the [right-exact tensor construction](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DF). The quotient is by N inside M; the coefficient coalgebra C is unchanged and need not be flat. Checks pass: [quotientCoact_comp_mkQ](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L87), [mkQ_eq_zero_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L233).
Checks the same relation as linear maps.
Checks precisely which vectors the projection kills.

The quotient comodule morphism sends m to its ordinary class modulo N. This defining formula adds no normalization or selection of representatives; the coaction is the one descended by [tensor right exactness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DF). It holds over the stated commutative ring without flatness of C, including the zero quotient when N is all of M. Checks pass: [mkQ_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L223), [mkQ_eq_zero_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L233).
Checks the complete underlying projection.
Checks its zero fibre is exactly N.

Real exponentiation on finite nonnegative reals agrees with exp(y·log x) when x>0. At zero, Lean sets 0^0=1 and 0^y=0 for every nonzero real exponent, including negative ones. This declaration installs the operation for real exponents; its zero convention differs from extended nonnegative reals, where negative powers of zero are infinity. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L40).

Computing a real power of a finite nonnegative real and then viewing the result as an ordinary real gives the same value as computing the ordinary real power directly. No sign condition on the exponent is needed. Both types share the zero defaults, including 0^0=1 and 0 raised to a negative exponent equalling zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L48).

A real power in finite nonnegative reals equals zero exactly when the base is zero and the exponent is nonzero. This includes negative exponents because Lean defines those powers of zero as zero in this finite type. At exponent zero every base gives 1, while a positive base always gives a positive value. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L58).

Every real power of a strictly positive finite nonnegative real is strictly positive, including zero and negative exponents. On this domain the power is an exponential, so it cannot vanish. Strict positivity of the base is sufficient for all exponents; allowing a zero base would fail for nonzero exponents under this type’s zero-power convention. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L343).

Extended nonnegative real powers use ordinary real exponentiation for positive finite bases. At base zero, positive, zero, and negative exponents give 0, 1, and ∞ respectively. At base ∞ they give ∞, 1, and 0. These explicit endpoint conventions extend the usual positive-base function; the exponent itself is always a finite real number. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L482).

The power notation for an extended nonnegative base and a real exponent uses the specified extended power function. In particular, 0^(−1)=∞, ∞^(−1)=0, and both 0^0 and ∞^0 equal 1. The exponent is a real number, not an extended value; this declaration installs an operation and does not itself assert unrestricted exponent laws. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L486).

Every extended nonnegative real raised to real exponent zero equals 1. The statement deliberately includes the endpoint cases 0^0=1 and ∞^0=1; these are the chosen values of the power function, not conclusions about limits where base and exponent vary together. No positivity or finiteness assumption on the base is required. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L494).

Raising an extended nonnegative real to real exponent 1 returns the base itself, including zero and infinity. On a positive finite base this is the ordinary identity x^1=x. The endpoint branches agree with it: zero to a positive exponent is zero, and infinity to a positive exponent is infinity. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L557).

Zero raised to a strictly positive real exponent is zero in the extended nonnegative reals. The exponent need not be an integer; positive fractional exponents are included. Its strict sign matters: at exponent zero the value is 1, and at a negative exponent the value is infinity. Those cases are separate branches of the definition. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L512).

Zero raised to a negative real exponent is infinity in the extended nonnegative reals. For example, 0^(−1)=∞. This differs from finite nonnegative real arithmetic, where the same zero-base negative power is defined as zero. The result records the extended endpoint convention; it does not give a finite reciprocal of zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L518).

Infinity raised to a positive real exponent remains infinity. This covers arbitrary positive real exponents, including fractions, and agrees with the growth of positive real powers as the base increases without bound. The strict positivity condition excludes the different assigned values at exponent zero, which gives 1, and at negative exponents, which give zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L505).

Infinity raised to a negative real exponent is zero. This matches the decay of reciprocal positive powers as their base grows without bound. The result concerns the assigned extended value, with a strictly negative finite real exponent. At exponent zero the value is instead 1, and positive exponents give infinity. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L508).

An extended nonnegative real power equals zero in exactly two cases: a zero base with positive exponent, or an infinite base with negative exponent. Positive finite bases never produce zero, and exponent zero always produces 1. This differs from the finite nonnegative type, where negative powers of zero are also assigned zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L570).

An extended nonnegative real power equals infinity exactly when its base is zero and its exponent negative, or its base is infinity and its exponent positive. No positive finite base can produce infinity at a real exponent. The zero-exponent case belongs to neither alternative because every zeroth power, including both endpoints, is 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L585).

A finite extended nonnegative base raised to a nonnegative real exponent cannot equal infinity. The base may be zero, and the exponent may be zero: positive powers of zero are zero, while 0^0 is 1. Dropping the exponent condition would permit the exceptional case of zero raised to a negative power, which is infinity. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L607).

For a finite extended nonnegative base and a nonnegative real exponent, the resulting power is strictly below infinity. Here “below infinity” means finite, not strictly positive: a zero base with positive exponent still gives zero. Exponent zero is allowed and gives 1, including at a zero base. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L615).

Every real power of a positive finite extended nonnegative base is finite. Unlike the nonnegative-exponent version, this statement allows negative exponents because the base excludes zero as well as infinity. These hypotheses are sufficient rather than necessary: some powers at excluded endpoints are finite too, such as 0^0=1 and ∞^(−1)=0. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L620).

Taking a power and converting its extended value to an ordinary real agrees with converting the base first and taking its real power. No guards are needed because the defaults align: both zero and infinity convert to zero, and ordinary zero to a negative power is zero. This equality does not certify finiteness of the extended result. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L959).

For a nonnegative real exponent, taking a power in finite nonnegative reals and then including it in the extended type agrees with taking the extended power directly. A zero base is allowed. The exponent guard prevents the mismatch at zero with negative exponent, where the finite type returns zero but the extended type returns infinity. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L542).

For a fixed nonnegative real exponent, increasing an extended nonnegative base cannot decrease its power. Zero and infinity are included. This is weak monotonicity: at exponent zero every base gives 1, so strict comparisons collapse. Negative exponents are excluded because on positive finite bases they reverse, rather than preserve, the order. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/NNReal.lean#L795).

Over a complete nonarchimedean field, a series distinguished in Y divides every overconvergent series uniquely as f=qg+r, with q overconvergent and r polynomial in Y. Distinguished means the coefficient in degree s is a unit attaining the Gauss norm, with later coefficients strictly smaller. The bound deg(r)<s uses deg(0)=−∞, so s=0 forces r=0. See [Grosse-Klönne §1.3(i), p.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1408.3329#page=3). Checks pass through existing families: [zero/constant and variable coefficients](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Dagger/OptionSeries.lean#L107); [Y+X² norm/radius calculations](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/TateAlgebra/Basic.lean#L251) and [substitution remainder](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Dagger/Subst.lean#L97); [zero excluded](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/GaussNorm.lean#L363), [one degree0](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/GaussNorm.lean#L515); [p-adic degrees and degree0 units](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Dagger/WashnitzerAlgebra.lean#L528), [linear analytic remainder](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/TateAlgebra/Eval.lean#L126); [one-variable maximum degree](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/GaussNorm.lean#L407). These are mathematical specializations, not separately compiled wrappers.
Division uses complete coefficient rings at unequal radii
The existing dagger substitution family computes Y+X² at Y=−X²
The weighted monomial norm calibrates equal and unequal radii
The existing linear family recognizes the degree-one case
The computed distinguished degrees cannot also be different degrees
The bounded analytic evaluation is the sum of monomial values
Degree-zero units retain their inverses in the overconvergent algebra

Over a complete nonarchimedean field K, every nonzero commutative algebra finite over Wₙ embeds Wₘ for some m≤n and is finite over that embedded algebra. Here Wₙ consists of power series converging beyond the unit polydisc; finite means finitely generated as a module through the displayed map. Nilpotents are retained, and n=0 gives W₀=K. See [Grosse-Klönne §1.4(2), p.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1408.3329#page=4). Checks pass: [zero variables](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Dagger/WashnitzerAlgebra.lean#L187), [finite relation elimination](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Dagger/Noetherian.lean#L87), [nilpotent residue quotients](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/RingTheory/Dagger/NoetherNormalization.lean#L150).
The zero-variable algebra is the coefficient ring
A finite map killing a distinguished relation remains finite after removing a variable
The finite-residue conclusion retains nilpotent thickenings

A local ring R containing a field and complete for its maximal-ideal powers admits a surjection κ[[Xᵢ]]→R for any finite generating family xᵢ of that ideal, where κ is the residue field. The map sends Xᵢ to xᵢ and lifts residue-field constants. That lift need not respect the originally specified field k; regularity is not assumed. See [Stacks, Theorem10.160.8 (032A)](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/032A). Checks pass by existing formulas: [ε evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/DualNumber/Polynomial.lean#L27) together with [power-series evaluation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Evaluation.lean#L175) and [low-coefficient divisibility](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Basic.lean#L513) computes the dual-number quotient; [no variables](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/Equiv.lean#L49) gives the field identity. These are mathematical specializations, not dedicated compiled quotient tests.
The constructed coefficient field splits the actual residue map
Evaluation sends prescribed generators and constants correctly and is surjective
The polynomial part of the existing epsilon evaluation keeps exactly constant and linear coefficients
The dual-number coordinate projection has the actual maximal ideal as kernel
